title: Supporting NumPy Across Major Versions
keywords: advanced numpy concepts and extension development
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of supporting numpy across major versions and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply detecting compatibility problems to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for supporting numpy across major versions.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 209 of the supplied curriculum: **Supporting NumPy Across Major Versions**. The main starting point is **Detecting compatibility problems**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Compiled extensions and stride-level operations can improve specialized workloads but increase portability and memory-safety complexity. Learn the high-level array contract first and keep extension paths narrowly tested.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Supporting NumPy Across Major Versions** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Detecting compatibility problems** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

version = np.lib.NumpyVersion(np.__version__)
print(version >= '2.0.0')
content_blocks.expected_output:
Observed output in the available validation environment (Python 3.13.5, NumPy 2.3.5):
True

common_mistakes.problem: Using low-level memory tools without validating strides and bounds
common_mistakes.why: Strided views and extension interfaces depend on layout and ownership contracts.
common_mistakes.fix: Start with safer high-level functions and add targeted tests before low-level paths.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming compiled binaries work across major NumPy versions
common_mistakes.why: The C API has binary-compatibility concerns across major versions.
common_mistakes.fix: Build/test wheels against supported NumPy versions and review migration notes.
